description:
FILED s462at (agent AT, round 19) as the ONE row of #934's matrix that is
measured and deliberately NOT shipped.

    package C; use overload '0+'=>sub{5}, '""'=>sub{"S"}, fallback => 1;
    my $x = C->new;          # no `+', no `++'
    $x++;

perl does NOT consult `0+' here.  With `fallback => 1' and nothing to
autogenerate from, it uses the ORDINARY (non-overloaded) semantics of the
operand -- for a blessed reference that is its ADDRESS -- and the result
REPLACES the scalar, so the blessing is GONE afterwards.  Probed 5.40.3:

    $x++;  print $x > 100 ? "big" : "small";   perl big     PCL small
    $x++;  print ref($x) || "-";               perl -       PCL C

PCL answers `0+' + 1 (so 6) and keeps the class.  #934 shipped the DEATH half
of the fallback rules and left this arm returning `(values nil nil)', which
routes to perl-increment's existing `0+' arm -- i.e. today's answer, unchanged.

WHY IT WAS LEFT, and it is not laziness: the VALUE alone is unobservable.
`box-set' leaves the class on the box, so after storing the address every
later read of $x goes back through `0+' and answers 5 again -- exactly what it
answers now.  Matching perl needs the DECLASSING, and that is a protocol change:
`p-pre++' / `p-post++' / `p-incf' / `p-incf-raw' all do
`(box-set place (perl-increment place))' and have no way to say "and this value
is a plain scalar now".  A two-value return from perl-increment (value +
plain-p), or a dedicated `%p-store-unblessed', is the shape.

WHERE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp `%p-incdec-autogen', the `((eq fallback t) (values
nil nil))' arm, whose comment points here.

BAR: the two probe rows above vs perl; the #934 rows in Pl/t/raw-verdict-01.t
unmoved (they assert the DEATHS, and `fb1++: ok' must stay ok); full sweep.

WORTH NOTING BEFORE SPENDING A SESSION ON IT: no real class relies on this.
A `fallback => 1' class with `0+' and no `+' that someone then INCREMENTS gets
a memory address in perl -- nobody writes that on purpose.  The reason to close
it is uniformity with #934, not a program that needs it.
subject: overload fallback => 1 with nothing to autogenerate: perl uses the ref ADDRESS and DROPS the blessing, PCL uses 0+ and keeps it (#934 residue)
